To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we can use a deep neural network to estimate interpratable statistics from visual observations, 2) we can train an agent to use these statistics for high-quality planning, and 3) we can generate natural language explanations for the agent’s actions that are high quality and useful for intervention.

(1) counterfactual explanations can be generated from a learned belief state, (2) the quality of these explanations can be improved by training the agent to generate explanations, and (3) the resulting agent is able to use these explanations to correct mistakes in a partially-revealed environment.

(a) counterfactual explanations of agent behavior can be used to improve agent behavior in the future and (b) a new training-by-explanning paradigm can be used to generate explanations of agent behavior in a partially-revealed world.
In summary, our research is concerned with
generating high quality natural language explanations of the reasoning behind the behavior of agents operating in partially-revealing environments.
how to explain high-level behavior to humans and how to learn to do so from experience.
how to generate natural-language explanations of high-level autonomous behavior, and how to train an agent to generate such explanations in a way that improves its own performance.
